newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain unions express doubts about 1998 budget.
newsitem.headline: Spain unions express doubts about 1998 budget.

text.p: Spain's leading trade union heads Antonio Gutierrez of the communist CCOO and Candido Mendez of the socialist UGT criticised the 1998 budget for lacking more serious measures to curtail unemployment.

"The government is determined to remain the flag bearer for cutbacks at the expense of keeping our country as the unemployment flag bearer with the highest rate in the EU," said Mendez, following a morning meeting with the government on the 1998 budget draft.

Gutierrez pointed out that according to the 1998 budget blue print the ministers presented during the meeting, unemployment benefits will be cut by 120 billion pesetas ($774 million) in 1998 while the latest INEM (employment institute) figures show payouts droppinig only 50 billion.
The CCOO secretary general said he had called for a new meeting with the Economy Minister for next September when "facts and figures" for next year's budget should be available.
Second-quarter Spanish unemployment fell to 20.94 percent from 21.49 percent in the first quarter.
The budget draft must be presented by the end of September. The government is expected to reveal details of the draft after Friday's cabinet meeting.
